doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: The Phantom CD and Ross's nickname
summary: Ross explains his nickname from Zoot Sims and how a letter at the Half Note made it stick.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: I know you’ve had some interesting recording experiences. You’ve made quite a few. In fact I have to ask you about one of your CDs here.
You look a little bit different here.
Well let’s see, that’s from 1993 or 92.
Oh, yes, that’s a nickname from many years ago.
Yeah? You want to tell us about it?
Zoot Sims, my friend Zoot Sims, he says “Ross can disappear in a phone booth.” Said “it’s amazing.”
“The Phantom.” And it re-surfaced after all this time.

Yeah. The gentleman that’s involved with that label, Progressive Records, Gus Statiras, who is a man with the thousands of records down in the lobby? He knew about that. He was around. There was a letter that came to me and it had my first name and then quotation marks The Phantom and then my last name, in care of the Half Note as a matter of fact, which was immediately put up like bulletin board style. And within a week, the jazz community in New York City in the 60s was very compact. Everybody knew everybody else. And within a week I was “The Phantom.”
